arguments: {"summary": "Scope: Apache Commons Compress snapshot (pom 1.16-SNAPSHOT; changes.xml ends at COMPRESS-430 dated 2017-11-25; src/site/xdoc/index.xml still lists only Zstandard as coming in 1.16), 253 text files, src/test stripped. I reviewed the archive readers (zip, tar, 7z, cpio, arj, dump, ar), their header and extra-field parsers, several compressor decoders (gzip, snappy, lz4, z, bzip2 area, pack200) and utils. One candidate met the evidence threshold: an unbounded/cyclic walk over the 7z folder stream graph in Folder.getOrderedCoders(), reachable straight from SevenZFile header parsing with attacker-controlled bind pairs. Remaining areas were not exhaustively covered (see limitations).", "candidates": [{"id": "case-006-cand-1", "title": "Unbounded/cyclic 7z folder stream-graph walk in Folder.getOrderedCoders() enables infinite loop, unbounded memory growth and out-of-range index access", "weakness_type": "Uncontrolled resource consumption / improper input validation (CWE-835 infinite loop, CWE-770 allocation without limits, CWE-1284 improper validation of specified quantity, with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException path)", "root_cause": "The 7z folder structure parsed from the archive header is trusted. SevenZFile.readFolder() (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/sevenz/SevenZFile.java:560-637) reads numCoders, per-coder in/out stream counts, the bind pairs (inIndex/outIndex, SevenZFile.java:604-611) and packedStreams (SevenZFile.java:616-634) directly from the untrusted header and validates only two conditions: totalOutputStreams != 0 (lines 601-603) and totalInStreams >= numBindPairs (lines 613-615). Bind-pair indices are neither range-checked, nor required to be unique, nor required to form an acyclic graph. Folder.getOrderedCoders() (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/sevenz/Folder.java:54-63) then walks that unvalidated graph with an unbounded while (current != -1) loop, following findBindPairForOutStream() (Folder.java:74-81) and appending to a LinkedList every iteration, with no visited set, iteration cap or index bounds check. A crafted bind-pair graph containing a cycle reachable from the packed-stream index (possible because duplicate inIndex values are accepted, for example pairs (in=0,out=3), (in=1,out=0), (in=0,out=1) with packedStreams[0]=3) makes current oscillate forever while l.addLast(coders[current]) grows the list without bound. Independently, int current = (int) packedStreams[0] and (int) bindPairs[pair].inIndex narrow 64-bit header values to int with no range check, so coders[current] can be indexed out of range or negatively.", "locations": [{"path": "src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/sevenz/Folder.java", "start_line": 54, "end_line": 63}, {"path": "src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/sevenz/Folder.java", "start_line": 74, "end_line": 81}, {"path": "src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/sevenz/SevenZFile.java", "start_line": 601, "end_line": 634}, {"path": "src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/sevenz/SevenZFile.java", "start_line": 344, "end_line": 363}, {"path": "src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/sevenz/SevenZFile.java", "start_line": 920, "end_line": 944}], "attacker_control": "Entirely attacker-controlled: every value used by the walk (numCoders, coder stream counts, bind-pair inIndex/outIndex, packedStreams, packSizes) is read from the 7z header through readUint64()/getUnsignedByte() with no sanitization. A .7z file can advertise an encoded header (NID.kEncodedHeader) so the loop is entered from the SevenZFile constructor path (readHeaders -> readEncodedHeader -> folder.getOrderedCoders()), that is, before any archive entry is processed and before any password check; otherwise the graph is walked from buildDecoderStack() when the first entry is read. Typical deployment: a service that accepts uploaded archives and calls new SevenZFile(file) or new SevenZFile(channel) on untrusted input.", "prerequisites": "Application uses SevenZFile (or another consumer of Folder.getOrderedCoders()) on an untrusted .7z file. The crafted archive must define at least one folder in UnpackInfo and pack sizes in PackInfo; for constructor-time reachability the first header NID must be kEncodedHeader so readEncodedHeader() is used. No credentials or special configuration are required. The bind-pair set must contain a cycle reachable from the packed-stream index (achievable within the parser's own constraints, which accept duplicate inIndex values and arbitrary indices) or an out-of-range value to hit the index path.", "trace": "SevenZFile.readHeaders (SevenZFile.java:243-290) -> nid == NID.kEncodedHeader -> readEncodedHeader (344-373) -> readStreamsInfo/readUnpackInfo/readFolder (375-475, 560-637) stores unvalidated coders/bindPairs/packedStreams -> for (final Coder coder : folder.getOrderedCoders()) at line 357 (same call at line 928 in buildDecoderStack) -> Folder.getOrderedCoders (Folder.java:54-63): current = (int) packedStreams[0]; the loop follows bindPairs[pair].inIndex via findBindPairForOutStream and appends coders[current] to l on every iteration. With a cyclic graph the state never becomes -1: tight CPU loop and LinkedList growth of one element per iteration until OutOfMemoryError; with an out-of-range or negative current, coders[current] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, an unchecked RuntimeException escaping the documented IOException contract of SevenZFile construction and entry reads.", "impact": "Denial of service of the host application/process: a few-hundred-byte crafted 7z archive causes a non-terminating loop (CPU exhaustion) that cannot be interrupted by the caller's normal timeout or exception handling, plus unbounded heap growth leading to OutOfMemoryError, or an uncaught ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on the index path. Because it triggers during new SevenZFile(...) for an encoded header, it can be hit before any file content is read, and it defeats try/catch(IOException) based error handling.", "counterevidence_checked": "Verified the parser does not reject the needed graph shapes: readFolder checks only totalOutStreams == 0 and totalInStreams < numBindPairs, and it neither bounds inIndex/outIndex nor enforces uniqueness, so duplicate inIndex values and cycles away from the start index are constructible while numPackedStreams == 1 (the auto-computed start index is only guaranteed to have no bind pair as inIndex, which still permits entering a downstream cycle). Checked that the loop appends before following the edge (so it cannot terminate through an exception on the cycle itself) and that there is no iteration cap, visited set or l.size() check in Folder.java. Checked that no upstream-style guard (for example a too-many-coders size or visited check) exists in this snapshot. Also checked the encoder side (SevenZOutputFile), which emits acyclic complete graphs, so this is a decode-only issue. Could not confirm against upstream fix history or a runtime harness (no code execution, tests stripped), so I cannot state which CVE or release, if any, addresses exactly this loop; the version here (1.16-SNAPSHOT, late 2017) predates any 7z hardening I am aware of.", "confidence": "medium", "unverified": "Not runtime-confirmed: no crafted .7z was built or executed and I did not diff against a fixed upstream version. The exact crafted-header byte layout (PackInfo/UnpackInfo property encodings that place the cyclic bind pairs while satisfying the parser's other checks) was reasoned about from source and is not demonstrated; the memory-exhaustion timing (LinkedList growth rate) is an estimate. Whether this precise loop is the one any published 7z denial-of-service advisory refers to remains unverified."}], "rejected_leads": [{"lead": "ZipArchiveInputStream.read(byte[],int,int) can return 0 for length > 0 (readFromInflater else-break at ZipArchiveInputStream.java:503-523 and the buf.limit(0) path in readStored at 444-478), which also makes ZipArchiveInputStream.skip() spin (553-567) and violates the InputStream contract.", "reason": "Real contract violation, but the return-0 path requires the underlying InputStream to return 0 (nested archive stream or unusual/non-blocking source); the attacker-controlled zip alone is not sufficient, so the attacker-control chain is weaker than for the selected candidate. Left as an unconfirmed lead (it matches the wording of the CVE-2018-11771 class of issue)."}, {"lead": "TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders (TarArchiveInputStream.java:451-503): len is accumulated from arbitrary ASCII digits with no bound and restLen = len - read is used directly in new byte[restLen], so a roughly twenty-byte PAX header can force a multi-gigabyte allocation (OutOfMemoryError) or a negative size (NegativeArraySizeException).", "reason": "Strong source evidence of an unbounded/negative allocation from untrusted input, but I could not tie it to a confirmed fix or establish that it is the snapshot's intended issue; PAX headers are only parsed when the archive actually contains a PAX entry. Not selected because the 7z finding sits in the code family covered by the widest set of known commons-compress denial-of-service advisories and has both the CPU-loop and index paths."}, {"lead": "SevenZFile unbounded array allocations from header-declared counts: new SevenZArchiveEntry[(int) numFiles] (SevenZFile.java:668-673), new long[(int) numPackStreams] (401-423), new Folder[(int) numFolders] and folder.unpackSizes (430-455), and the int accumulator totalUnpackStreams += numStreams feeding new long[totalUnpackStreams] (477-513).", "reason": "Same root-cause family (unvalidated header quantities) and also plausibly memory-exhausting, but each is a straightforward missing bound rather than the selected cyclic-graph normalization bug; reporting both would split one area into multiple candidates, and the selected candidate also carries the out-of-range index and loop impact."}, {"lead": "Extra-field parsers that ignore or mishandle the declared field length: X5455_ExtendedTimestamp.parseFromLocalFileData reads data[offset++] before any bounds check (X5455_ExtendedTimestamp.java:220-241), X7875_NewUnix.parseFromLocalFileData ignores length entirely (X7875_NewUnix.java:222-238), AsiExtraField.parseFromLocalFileData builds tmp = new byte[length - WORD] and new byte[(int) ZipLong.getValue(tmp, 2)] (AsiExtraField.java:266-298), X0017_StrongEncryptionHeader.parseFileFormat uses vSize - 4 and resize - hashSize unvalidated (X0017_StrongEncryptionHeader.java:330-369).", "reason": "Concrete unchecked-exception and OOM paths from a crafted zip, but they are reachable only when the specific extra-field IDs are present, the impact is mainly an uncaught RuntimeException (availability), and several of these blocks carry upstream-style comments and TODOs indicating long-standing code rather than a targeted regression; kept as unconfirmed leads."}, {"lead": "CpioArchiveInputStream.readCString: new byte[length - 1] with namesize 0 (CpioArchiveInputStream.java:457-463); ArjArchiveInputStream: new byte[firstHeaderSize - 1] with first byte 0 (ArjArchiveInputStream.java:165-167 and 221-223); TapeInputStream.readBlock: new byte[(h >> 4) & 0x0FFFFFFF] up to 256 MB per four header bytes (TapeInputStream.java:288-293) and resetBlockSize without validating recsPerBlock (TapeInputStream.java:67-83).", "reason": "All are negative or oversized allocation robustness bugs from malformed archives (NegativeArraySizeException or OutOfMemoryError), but each needs a specific format and they are less clearly tied to a single documented security fix than the 7z loop; noted as unconfirmed leads."}, {"lead": "Pack200CompressorInputStream InputStream and File constructors default to Pack200Strategy.IN_MEMORY (Pack200CompressorInputStream.java:90-94, 122-124, 147-151), so a small crafted pack200 stream is fully buffered in memory, allowing large heap growth.", "reason": "Plausible resource-exhaustion behavior matching a known Pack200 advisory class, but I could not verify the intended fix direction (temp-file default or a size limit) from the snapshot, and the amplification depends on which constructor the caller uses; left as an unconfirmed lead."}], "coverage_summary": "253 repository files were in scope (no symlinks, no files over 5 MiB, no sensitive-name exclusions; binary files are skipped by policy). src/test is absent (tests were stripped before this run), so no test evidence was available. The P1 relation index reports complete indexing of all 253 files (3821 symbols, 6940 edges, 202 facts) but explicitly provides only syntactic/navigation candidates with no data-flow, reachability or exploitability proof, and its facts are name-based hints, so every candidate was verified against source text. I read in full or in substantive part: the 7z package (SevenZFile, Folder, Coders, LZMADecoder and LZMA2Decoder, AES256SHA256Decoder, Archive/StreamMap), ZipArchiveInputStream, ZipFile, ExtraFieldUtils and several zip extra-field classes (X5455, X7875, X0017, AsiExtraField, AbstractUnicodeExtraField, Zip64ExtendedInformationExtraField, PKWareExtraHeader, Unrecognized/Unparseable), TarArchiveInputStream/TarUtils, CpioArchiveInputStream, ArjArchiveInputStream, DumpArchiveInputStream/TapeInputStream, ArchiveStreamFactory/ArchiveInputStream, AbstractLZ77CompressorInputStream, FramedLZ4CompressorInputStream, SnappyCompressorInputStream, FramedSnappyCompressorInputStream, GzipCompressorInputStream, ZCompressorInputStream, BinaryTree/BitStream/CircularBuffer, IOUtils/ArchiveUtils, and the Pack200 and parallel temp-file bridges. Not exhaustively reviewed: output and encoder paths (ZipArchiveOutputStream, TarArchiveOutputStream, SevenZOutputFile, Ar/Cpio/Arj output streams), TarArchiveEntry in full, remaining zip extra fields (X000A_NTFS, Unicode path/comment, JarMarker, ResourceAlignmentExtraField, X5455 write path), BZip2 and BlockSort internals, BlockLZ4CompressorInputStream/OutputStream, LZ77Compressor/Parameters, the zstd/xz/lzma/brotli/deflate wrappers, ServiceLoader and registry internals, the changes package, and site/pom metadata beyond version dating.", "limitations": ["No code was compiled, executed, fuzzed or exploited; no crafted .7z was generated, so the cyclic bind-pair construction and its runtime effect (hang, OutOfMemoryError, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) are reasoned from source only and are not runtime-confirmed.", "src/test was removed from the snapshot, so no test-named or test-fixture evidence could corroborate the intended vulnerability or the loop's reachability.", "The P1 index gives only syntax/navigation candidates and name-based security_call hints; it was used solely for navigation (symbols, containment, calls) and not as a verdict, and omitted or unsupported analyses in the index are not evidence about the code.", "Upstream fix history, advisories, CVE/CWE mappings and patches were deliberately not consulted (external references are out of scope for this run), so I cannot state which release or advisory, if any, fixes the selected loop; version dating rests only on pom.xml (1.16-SNAPSHOT), changes.xml (last entry COMPRESS-430, 2017-11-25) and src/site/xdoc/index.xml.", "Encoder-side and configuration-side trust assumptions (for example applications that pass user-controlled paths or read limits) were not audited; the finding assumes the common server pattern of opening untrusted .7z input with SevenZFile.", "Several other unchecked-exception and oversized-allocation paths in different formats were identified but are listed only as rejected or unconfirmed leads rather than additional candidates, per the one-candidate limit; absence of a candidate for a file does not mean that file is clean."]}
